summary: The proposal addresses a relevant and well-scoped problem (connecting Artemis with GitLab CI for dynamic build plans) and demonstrates domain knowledge, but it is missing multiple required sections entirely (Introduction, Motivation, Objective, AI Transparency Statement), has only one figure which is a prohibited type, falls short on bibliography entries, and presents the schedule as a waterfall timeline rather than iterative sprints. Writing issues are pervasive (passive voice, filler words, forbidden sentence starters, inconsistent terminology), and the document is below the minimum page length. Substantial restructuring and rewriting are needed before this can be considered submission-ready.

findings.title: Missing Introduction section
findings.description: The proposal does not contain a dedicated Introduction section. The document transitions directly from the Abstract to '1 Problem Statement'. An Introduction section is required and must be less than one page.

locations.quote: **1     Problem          Statement**

findings.title: Missing Motivation section
findings.description: The proposal does not contain a standalone Motivation section as required by the guidelines. While positive aspects (e.g., more universities adopting Artemis, saving time/money, new research opportunities) are scattered in 'Expected Findings' (Section 5) and the visionary scenario in Section 4, there is no dedicated section that is visionary, explains why it is scientifically important to solve the problem, and focuses on the positive vision of having the solution. The Motivation section must be added as a separate, clearly labeled section of at most 3/4 page.

findings.title: Missing Objective section with required subsections
findings.description: The proposal lacks an 'Objective' section structured as required: a short introduction, a bullet list of 3-4 high-level objectives (each fitting in one line), and a subsection for each objective (at least two paragraphs long). The 'Expected Findings' section is framed as expectations ('We expect to use...', 'might be extended') rather than action-form objectives, and no subsections with detailed descriptions are present. All objectives must be reformulated in action form (e.g., 'Extend the Artemis API to expose build plans' rather than 'The API of Artemis might be extended').

locations.quote: **4     System        Requirements              and     Top     Level     Design**
This research thesis **deals with the question on how to connect** Artemis with GitLab CI. We **expect to use** the bridge pattern, described by Gamma et al.
For making the build plan accessible, the API of Artemis **might be extended** for this service.

findings.title: AI Transparency Statement is entirely missing
findings.description: The proposal does not contain an AI Transparency Statement. The guidelines explicitly require this section. It must be written in the first person, name specific AI tools used, state the purpose of each tool, identify which sections they were applied to, and include a sentence confirming the author has carefully checked all AI-generated text. As the section is entirely absent, none of these requirements can be evaluated or satisfied.

findings.title: Schedule is not structured into 2-4 week iterations
findings.description: The schedule is organized as a month-by-month linear timeline with sporadic week references (e.g., '2nd week', '4th week') rather than clearly defined 2-4 week iterations/sprints. There is no grouping of work into discrete iterative cycles. The entire schedule reads as a waterfall Gantt-chart timeline from March to December, not as a series of 2-4 week iterations with clear boundaries.

findings.title: Figure 1 is a sequence diagram, which is explicitly prohibited
findings.description: Figure 1 depicts two actors (Instructor, Student) with numbered point-to-point messages (1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3) exchanged vertically, which is the structure of a UML sequence diagram. Since this is the core concept of the proposal, a single consistent term (e.g., "CI server" for standalone systems and "CI service" only when specifically referring to the integrated GitLab CI component) should be used throughout the author's own prose.

findings.title: Paragraph exceeds 10 lines and covers multiple unrelated ideas
findings.description: The paragraph beginning 'In their paper Interactive Learning…' spans from page 2 into page 3, making it well over 10 rendered lines. It also compresses at least three distinct ideas into a single paragraph: (a) the interactive learning concept and its purpose, (b) the specific shortening of the theory-practice gap, and (c) the lecture phase structure and its connection to Artemis. This paragraph should be split into two or three shorter paragraphs, each developing one idea.

locations.quote: In their paper Interactive Learning – Increasing Student Participation through Shorter Exercise Cycles, Krusche et al. have taken up this concept to improve the learning experience in large computer science courses at university [Krusche17]. They introduced an newly developed learning method which shortens the time between theory...

**into multiple iterations, each consisting of different phases [Krusche17]. First there is a theory phase, before the instructor shows an example to the students. After that the students can try out the concept themselves, before they get a sample solution and instant, but still individual feedback generated by the CI server. Afterwards it is possible to reflect about the newly learned approach. With this fundamental idea, later the assessment management system Artemis was built [Krusche18].**

findings.title: Requirements-gathering task included in schedule
findings.description: The schedule explicitly lists 'Requirements' as a work item in June (parallel to prototype implementation). Per agile principles, there should not be a dedicated requirements-gathering phase; work items are selected from a backlog each iteration. This violates the rule against a requirements sprint.

findings.title: Work items follow horizontal layer splits rather than vertically integrated features
findings.description: The prototype work is split into horizontal layers: first 'Connectivity to GitLab CI' (April), then 'Artemis API for configuration' (May), then 'Sending build results to Artemis' (June), with 'Models' as a separate parallel track. This is a classic horizontal decomposition (build all networking, then all API, then all data flow) rather than vertically integrated end-to-end features. A vertically integrated approach would deliver, for example, a minimal working exercise submission cycle end-to-end in the first iteration, then extend it.
